title: Pythagorean Theorem: Building from Triples
preview: Warm up with squaring and square roots, then thin-slice Pythagorean. Hypotenuse first, then legs, then irrational answers.

body.goal: Students build fluency with a² + b² = c² by walking through carefully chosen triangles — Pythagorean triples first, then non-triple cases that force a square root.
body.launch: Run the warm-up first so squaring and square-rooting are ready. Then introduce the formula and start the slice. Don't draw triangles for them — let groups draw their own.
body.stem: Right triangle: a² + b² = c²  (a, b are legs; c is the hypotenuse)
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up by squaring numbers and finding square roots before we use them in the theorem.

prerequisiteSteps.teacherNote: Less familiar — let groups guess and check rather than memorize.

steps.teacherNote: Same triple, doubled. Some groups will spot this and skip the arithmetic.
Another triple. Pattern recognition is fine — the goal is fluency.
First irrational answer. Push: 'It's not a whole number — did we mess up?' (No — exact answer is √2.)
Another irrational. Resist decimal approximation — exact answer is √13.

body.consolidation: Ask: 'When does the hypotenuse come out a whole number? When doesn't it?' Pull out: only Pythagorean triples (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, etc.) give whole hypotenuses. Everything else is irrational — and that's a perfectly fine answer.
